For example, $\\dfrac{7}{15}$ is a little less than $\\dfrac{1}{2}$, because half of $15$ is $7.5$ and $7<7.5$."},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"Quick test against one half","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A positive fraction $\\dfrac{a}{b}$ is less than $\\dfrac{1}{2}$ when $2a<b$, equal to $\\dfrac{1}{2}$ when $2a=b$, and greater than $\\dfrac{1}{2}$ when $2a>b$. This week we use all of these forms and move freely between them."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Adding and subtracting in real contexts","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Parts can only be added when they are the same size, so first rewrite the fractions over a common denominator (best of all, the LCM of the denominators). For example, $\\dfrac{9}{10}$ kg of seed fills $\\dfrac{9}{10}\\div\\dfrac{3}{40}=12$ bags of $\\dfrac{3}{40}$ kg."},{"k":"fig","id":"w05-bags","caption":"$\\frac{9}{10}$ kg is $\\frac{36}{40}$ kg, which makes 12 groups of $\\frac{3}{40}$ kg."},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Cancel factors, not terms","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Cancel common **factors** before multiplying to keep the numbers small: $\\dfrac{7}{12}\\times\\dfrac{15}{14}=\\dfrac{1\\times5}{4\\times2}$ after cancelling $7$ and $3$. Zeros at the **end** of a decimal do not change its value: $0.6=0.60=0.600$."},{"k":"p","text":"To change a terminating decimal into a fraction, use the place value of the last digit as the denominator, then simplify:"},{"k":"math","tex":"0.625=\\frac{625}{1000}=\\frac{5}{8}"}],"figs":["w05-placevalue"]},{"title":"Recurring decimals","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"To change a fraction into a decimal, divide the numerator by the denominator. This is a proof, not a guess."},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"When only part of the decimal repeats","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"For $x=0.8\\dot{3}$, first move the non-repeating digit: $10x=8.333\\ldots$ and $100x=83.333\\ldots$ Subtracting gives $90x=75$, so $x=\\dfrac{75}{90}=\\dfrac{5}{6}$."}]}],"figs":["w05-longdiv"]},{"title":"Additive inverses","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The **additive inverse** of a number is the number you add to it to get $0$. They are three ways of writing **the same number**:"},{"k":"ul","items":["a **fraction** shows the part–whole relationship, e.g. $\\dfrac{3}{8}$;","a **decimal** shows base-ten place value, e.g. $0.375$;","a **percentage** shows the amount per hundred, e.g. $37.5\\%$."]},{"k":"fig","id":"w06-three","caption":"Each eighth lines up with a decimal and a percentage. Shading 25 squares shows $\\dfrac{25}{100}=\\dfrac{1}{4}=0.25=25\\%$."},{"k":"fig","id":"w06-hundred","caption":"Left: 25 of 100 squares is one quarter. Right: the grid in five equal groups of 20; three groups make $\\frac{3}{5}=60\\%$."},{"k":"p","text":"Learn these **benchmarks** by their meaning, not just their symbols. They make estimation quick and reliable."},{"k":"table","head":["Fraction","Decimal","Percentage"],"rows":[["$\\dfrac{1}{2}$","$0.5$","$50\\%$"],["$\\dfrac{1}{4}$","$0.25$","$25\\%$"],["$\\dfrac{3}{4}$","$0.75$","$75\\%$"],["$\\dfrac{1}{5}$","$0.2$","$20\\%$"],["$\\dfrac{1}{10}$","$0.1$","$10\\%$"],["$\\dfrac{1}{8}$","$0.125$","$12.5\\%$"],["$\\dfrac{1}{3}$","$0.\\dot{3}$","$33\\dfrac{1}{3}\\%$"]]}],"figs":["w06-hundred"]},{"title":"Decimals to fractions","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"For a decimal with $n$ digits after the point, write the digits (without the point) over $10^n$, then simplify:"},{"k":"math","tex":"0.0375=\\frac{375}{10000}=\\frac{3}{80}\\qquad\\qquad1.125=\\frac{1125}{1000}=\\frac{9}{8}=1\\frac{1}{8}"},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"Zeros in decimals","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["Zeros at the **end** do not change the value: $0.4=0.40=0.400$.","Zeros straight **after the point** do change it: $0.04$ is ten times smaller than $0.4$, because the $4$ has moved from the tenths place to the hundredths place."]}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Fractions and percentages","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"To write $\\dfrac{a}{b}$ as a percentage, multiply by $100\\%$:"},{"k":"math","tex":"\\frac{7}{16}\\times100\\%=\\frac{700}{16}\\%=43.75\\%"},{"k":"p","text":"Notice that $0.4375$ is the decimal and $43.75\\%$ is the percentage. Only write the $\\%$ sign on a percentage."},{"k":"p","text":"A percentage can be **more than** $100\\%$ when the amount is larger than the whole: $\\dfrac{9}{8}=1.125=112.5\\%$."},{"k":"p","text":"To change a percentage into a fraction, divide by $100$ and simplify: $62.5\\%=0.625=\\dfrac{625}{1000}=\\dfrac{5}{8}$. If the percentage itself contains a fraction, deal with that first:"},{"k":"math","tex":"33\\frac{1}{3}\\%=\\frac{100}{3}\\%=\\frac{100}{3}\\times\\frac{1}{100}=\\frac{1}{3}"}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Rounding and estimation","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"To round $0.37684$ to three decimal places, keep $0.376$ and look at the **next** digit, $8$. Since it is $5$ or more, round up to $0.377$, which is about $37.7\\%$."},{"k":"fig","id":"w06-rounding","caption":"$0.37684$ lies past the halfway point $0.3765$, so it is nearer to $0.377$."},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Round only at the end","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Rounding in the middle of a calculation adds small errors that can grow. Keep exact values (or extra decimal places) until the final answer, then round as the question asks."}]},{"k":"p","text":"Use benchmarks to check answers. $\\dfrac{7}{15}$ is a little less than $\\dfrac{1}{2}$, so it must be a little less than $50\\%$; an answer of $4.7\\%$ or $470\\%$ is clearly wrong. (In fact $\\dfrac{7}{15}=46.\\dot{6}\\%$.)"}],"figs":["w06-rounding"]},{"title":"Percentage of an amount, and finding the whole","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"**Percentage of an amount.** Change the percentage into a fraction or decimal and multiply:"},{"k":"math","tex":"35\\%\\text{ of }240=\\frac{35}{100}\\times240=84"},{"k":"p","text":"So $35\\%$ of GH₵240 is GH₵84."},{"k":"p","text":"**Finding the whole.** If GH₵84 is $35\\%$ of a total, then $1\\%$ is $84\\div35=2.40$, so $100\\%$ is GH₵240. In one step: total $=84\\div0.35=$ GH₵240."},{"k":"fig","id":"w06-whole","caption":"The bar is the whole (100%). Knowing that 35% is GH₵84 lets us find 1% and then 100%."},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"Ask: which quantity is missing?","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Every percentage problem links three things: the **percentage**, the **part** and the **whole**."},{"k":"math","tex":"\\text{part}=\\text{percentage}\\times\\text{whole}"},{"k":"p","text":"Decide which one the question asks for before you calculate."}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w06-budget","caption":"A budget of GH₵1,280: $37.5\\%=\\frac{3}{8}$ goes to food and the remaining $62.5\\%=\\frac{5}{8}$ to other needs (Worked Example 6.4)."},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"Percentage points","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"If an estimate of $45\\%$ should have been $43.75\\%$, the error is $45-43.75=1.25$ **percentage points**. Percentage points measure the gap between two percentages; they are not the same as a percentage change."}]}],"figs":["w06-whole","w06-budget"]},{"title":"Inverses in every form","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Inverses work the same way whatever the form. For $\\dfrac{3}{8}=0.375=37.5\\%$:"},{"k":"ul","items":["the **additive inverse** is $-\\dfrac{3}{8}=-0.375$, because the sum is $0$;","the **reciprocal** is $\\dfrac{8}{3}$, because $\\dfrac{3}{8}\\times\\dfrac{8}{3}=1=100\\%$."]},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"A strategy for harder problems","blocks":[{"k":"ol","items":["Identify the whole.","Choose the most useful form (fraction, decimal or percentage).","Work without unnecessary rounding.","Convert back to the form and units the question asks for, and check that the answer is reasonable."]}]}],"figs":[]}],"examples":[{"title":"One share in three forms","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A community library owns 640 textbooks, of which 248 are mathematics textbooks. <script type="application/json" id="pack-y1w07">{"year":1,"week":7,"id":"y1w07","title":"Applications of Percentages in Household Finance","subtitle":"Percentage increase and decrease, multipliers, discounts, reverse percentages, profit and loss, commission, tax and household budgets.","family":"number","section":{"no":1,"name":"Number","strand":"Number for Everyday Life","from":1,"to":8},"outcomes":["Calculate percentage increase, percentage decrease and discounts from the correct original amount.","Use multipliers, and solve reverse-percentage problems to find an original price.","Calculate profit, loss, commission and tax in household and business contexts.","Explain why successive percentage changes are multiplied, not added.","Compare offers and budgets and interpret the answers in context."],"keywords":["percentage change","multiplier","discount","marked price","selling price","cost price","profit","loss","commission","tax","reverse percentage"],"notes":[{"title":"Percentages in money problems","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A percentage means “parts in every hundred”. So $15\\%$ means 15 out of every 100, not GH₵15 (unless the original amount is GH₵100). In every money question, first identify the **original amount**, the base on which the percentage is taken."},{"k":"p","text":"There are three different tasks:"},{"k":"ol","items":["finding a percentage **of** a known amount;","finding what percentage one amount is **of another**;","finding the **original** amount when the changed amount is known."]},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Percentage change","blocks":[{"k":"math","tex":"\\text{percentage change}=\\frac{\\text{change}}{\\text{original}}\\times100\\%"},{"k":"p","text":"For an increase the change is $\\text{new}-\\text{original}$; for a decrease it is $\\text{original}-\\text{new}$."}]},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Always divide by the original","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The most common examination error is dividing by the **new** amount. If a price rises from GH₵450 to GH₵540, the increase is $\\dfrac{90}{450}\\times100\\%=20\\%$, not $\\dfrac{90}{540}\\times100\\%$."}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Multipliers: the quickest reliable method","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The original amount is $100\\%$, which is a multiplier of $1$."},{"k":"ul","items":["A $12\\%$ **increase** gives $100\\%+12\\%=112\\%$ of the original, so multiply by $1.12$.","A $12\\%$ **decrease** gives $100\\%-12\\%=88\\%$ of the original, so multiply by $0.88$."]},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Multipliers","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["Increase by $r\\%$: $\\;\\text{new}=\\text{original}\\times\\left(1+\\dfrac{r}{100}\\right)$","Decrease by $r\\%$: $\\;\\text{new}=\\text{original}\\times\\left(1-\\dfrac{r}{100}\\right)$","Reverse: $\\;\\text{original}=\\text{new}\\div\\text{multiplier}$"]}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w07-multiplier","caption":"To undo a percentage change, divide by the same multiplier. Adding 15% back to the reduced price does not give the original."},{"k":"p","text":"For example, a price of GH₵896 after a $20\\%$ reduction is $80\\%$ of the original, so the original is $896\\div0.80=$ GH₵1,120, **not** $896\\times1.20$."}],"figs":["w07-multiplier"]},{"title":"Discount, marked price and selling price","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["The **marked price** is the price on the tag before any reduction.","The **discount** is the amount taken off: $\\text{discount}=\\text{rate}\\times\\text{marked price}$.","The **selling price** is what the customer pays: $\\text{marked price}-\\text{discount}$."]},{"k":"fig","id":"w07-discount","caption":"After a 20% discount the customer pays 80% of the marked price. The part paid and the discount together make 100%."},{"k":"p","text":"**Successive discounts** are applied one after the other, each to the price at that moment. A $20\\%$ discount followed by a $10\\%$ discount gives a combined multiplier of $0.80\\times0.90=0.72$: a total reduction of $28\\%$, not $30\\%$."},{"k":"fig","id":"w07-successive","caption":"The second discount is 10% of GH₵1,200, not of GH₵1,500, so the total discount is 28%."},{"k":"box","kind":"note","title":"Order matters","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A fixed GH₵30 coupon used after a $15\\%$ discount is not the same as a further $15\\%$ off. Follow the order given in the question and write down each intermediate amount."}]}],"figs":["w07-discount","w07-successive"]},{"title":"Profit and loss","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The **cost price** (CP) is the total cost of buying an item and getting it ready for sale, including transport, repairs or packaging when these are given. The **selling price** (SP) is what the buyer pays."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Profit and loss","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["Profit $=\\text{SP}-\\text{CP}$ (when SP is greater than CP)","Loss $=\\text{CP}-\\text{SP}$ (when SP is less than CP)","$\\text{Profit }\\%=\\dfrac{\\text{profit}}{\\text{CP}}\\times100\\%$ and $\\text{Loss }\\%=\\dfrac{\\text{loss}}{\\text{CP}}\\times100\\%$"]}]},{"k":"p","text":"Profit and loss percentages are worked out on the **cost price**. A trader who buys for GH₵400 and sells for GH₵500 makes GH₵100 profit, which is $25\\%$ of the cost price, even though it is only $20\\%$ of the selling price."},{"k":"fig","id":"w07-profit","caption":"The same GH₵100 profit is 25% of the cost price but 20% of the selling price. Profit percentage always uses the cost price."},{"k":"p","text":"For a $15\\%$ profit, $\\text{SP}=1.15\\times\\text{CP}$; for a $15\\%$ loss, $\\text{SP}=0.85\\times\\text{CP}$. To find the cost price from the selling price, divide by the multiplier."}],"figs":["w07-profit"]},{"title":"Commission, tax and bills","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"**Commission** is payment for making sales: $\\text{commission}=\\text{rate}\\times\\text{qualifying sales}$. A salesperson may get a fixed salary **plus** commission; work out the two parts separately and add them."},{"k":"p","text":"**Tax** is calculated on a stated amount (the tax base). If a $10\\%$ tax is added after a discount, find the discounted price first, then add $10\\%$ of that amount."},{"k":"box","kind":"note","title":"About the tax rates","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The tax rates in this lesson are examples given in each question. They are not a statement of Ghana’s current tax rules."}]},{"k":"p","text":"**Household bills** often have a fixed charge plus a charge for each unit used. Show the units and the GH₵ sign, and round money to two decimal places only at the end."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Comparing offers and budgets","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Compare the **final amounts** you would pay, not the size of the percentage in the advertisement. Check whether delivery fees, tax or conditions are included."},{"k":"fig","id":"w07-budget","caption":"A budget shown as a 100% bar. The parts allocated and the part left over must add up to 100%."},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"Writing a complete solution","blocks":[{"k":"ol","items":["List the known amounts and identify the original amount.","Write the relationship (formula or multiplier).","Substitute and calculate, showing each step.","Check the answer another way, and finish with a sentence that explains what it means."]}]}],"figs":["w07-budget"]}],"examples":[{"title":"A discounted laptop","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A laptop was marked at GH₵4,800. During a promotion the price was reduced by $17.5\\%$. Find (a) the discount and (b) the amount the customer paid."}],"steps":["Rate: $17.5\\%=0.175$.","Discount: $0.175\\times4800=840$, so the discount is GH₵840.","Selling price: $4800-840=3960$, so the customer pays GH₵3,960.","Check with the multiplier: $1-0.175=0.825$ and $0.825\\times4800=3960$ ✓."],"answer":"(a) GH₵840 (b) GH₵3,960","figs":[]},{"title":"Finding the original price","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A school paid GH₵1,020 for an item after a $15\\%$ discount. Find the marked price. A learner says it is GH₵1,173 because “15% is added back”. Explain the error."}],"steps":["After the discount the school paid $100\\%-15\\%=85\\%$ of the marked price $P$.","$0.85P=1020$, so $P=1020\\div0.85=1200$.","Check: $15\\%$ of $1200$ is $180$, and $1200-180=1020$ ✓.","The learner found $15\\%$ of the **reduced** price ($1020\\times1.15=1173$), but the discount was $15\\%$ of the **original** price."],"answer":"The marked price was GH₵1,200. A reverse percentage is found by dividing by the multiplier.","figs":[]},{"title":"Profit on calculators","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A trader buys 18 calculators at GH₵85 each and pays GH₵90 for transport. All 18 are sold at GH₵110 each. Find the profit and the percentage profit on the total cost."}],"steps":["Purchase cost: $18\\times85=1530$.","Total cost price: $1530+90=1620$.","Sales: $18\\times110=1980$.","Profit: $1980-1620=360$.","Profit percentage: $\\dfrac{360}{1620}\\times100\\%=22.22\\%$ (2 d.p.)."],"answer":"Profit GH₵360; percentage profit $22.22\\%$.","figs":[]},{"title":"Selling at a loss","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A trader sells a refrigerator for GH₵2,760 at a loss of $8\\%$ on the cost. Find the cost price and the loss."}],"steps":["An $8\\%$ loss means $\\text{SP}=92\\%$ of the cost price $C$.","$0.92C=2760$, so $C=2760\\div0.92=3000$.","Loss: $3000-2760=240$.","Check: $8\\%$ of $3000=240$ ✓."],"answer":"Cost price GH₵3,000; loss GH₵240.","figs":[]},{"title":"Salary plus commission","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A sales representative earns a fixed salary of GH₵1,250 plus $4\\%$ commission on sales **above** GH₵8,000. Total sales are GH₵22,500. Find the monthly earnings."}],"steps":["Qualifying sales: $22500-8000=14500$.","Commission: $0.04\\times14500=580$.","Earnings: $1250+580=1830$.","Commission is not paid on the full GH₵22,500, because the question says “above GH₵8,000”."],"answer":"GH₵1,830","figs":[]},{"title":"Discount, then tax","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A washing machine costing GH₵3,200 gets a $12\\%$ discount. A $10\\%$ sales tax is then added to the discounted price. Find the final amount paid."}],"steps":["Discount: $0.12\\times3200=384$.","Discounted price: $3200-384=2816$.","Tax: $0.10\\times2816=281.60$.","Final amount: $2816+281.60=3097.60$.","Check with multipliers: $3200\\times0.88\\times1.10=3097.60$ ✓."],"answer":"GH₵3,097.60","figs":[]},{"title":"Two discounts in a row","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A shop gives “$20\\%$ off today and another $10\\%$ off tomorrow” on the reduced price. A chair originally costs GH₵1,500. Find the final price and the total reduction as a percentage of the original price."}],"steps":["After the first discount: $1500\\times0.80=1200$.","After the second discount: $1200\\times0.90=1080$.","Total reduction: $1500-1080=420$.","Percentage: $\\dfrac{420}{1500}\\times100\\%=28\\%$.","It is not $30\\%$, because the second $10\\%$ is taken from GH₵1,200, not GH₵1,500."],"answer":"Final price GH₵1,080; total discount $28\\%$.","figs":[]},{"title":"A household budget","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A family has GH₵2,400 a month for expenses. Find the amount not yet allocated and its percentage."}],"steps":["Allocated: $35\\%+22.5\\%+17.5\\%=75\\%$.","Not allocated: $100\\%-75\\%=25\\%$.","Amount: $0.25\\times2400=600$.","Check: $0.75\\times2400=1800$ and $2400-1800=600$ ✓."],"answer":"$25\\%$ of the budget, which is GH₵600.","figs":[]}],"summary":[{"title":"Key results for Week 7","items":["$\\text{Percentage change}=\\dfrac{\\text{change}}{\\text{original}}\\times100\\%$","Increase by $r\\%$: multiply by $1+\\dfrac{r}{100}$. <script type="application/json" id="pack-y1w08">{"year":1,"week":8,"id":"y1w08","title":"Simple and Compound Interest and Financial Growth","subtitle":"Principal, rate, time and amount; simple interest and its reverse problems; compound interest with annual, half-yearly and quarterly compounding; depreciation and growth factors.","family":"number","section":{"no":1,"name":"Number","strand":"Number for Everyday Life","from":1,"to":8},"outcomes":["Explain principal, rate, time, interest, amount and compounding period.","Use the simple-interest formula, and rearrange it to find the principal, rate or time.","Calculate compound interest year by year and with the formula, including half-yearly and quarterly compounding.","Use growth and decay factors for depreciation and successive percentage changes.","Compare savings and loan options and interpret the results."],"keywords":["principal","interest rate","simple interest","compound interest","amount","compounding period","growth factor","depreciation","effective rate"],"notes":[{"title":"The meaning of interest","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"When you borrow money you usually pay an extra charge called **interest**; when you save or invest money you may **earn** interest."},{"k":"box","kind":"definition","title":"Key terms","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["**Principal** $P$: the money first saved or borrowed.","**Rate** $r\\%$: the percentage charged or earned per stated period, usually per year (per annum, p.a.).","**Time** $t$: how long the money is saved or borrowed, in the same unit as the rate.","**Interest** $I$: the extra money earned or paid.","**Amount** $A$: the total at the end, $A=P+I$."]}]},{"k":"p","text":"If the rate is per year, the time must be in years. For example, $9$ months $=\\dfrac{9}{12}=0.75$ year and $30$ months $=\\dfrac{30}{12}=2.5$ years."},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Read the question","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The question must say whether the interest is **simple** or **compound**. Do not assume compound interest just because a bank is involved."}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Simple interest","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"**Simple interest** is calculated on the original principal only. The interest is the same every year, so the amount grows in a straight line."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Simple interest","blocks":[{"k":"math","tex":"I=\\frac{P\\times r\\times t}{100}\\qquad\\qquad A=P+I"},{"k":"p","text":"$P$ in cedis, $r$ the percentage rate per year, $t$ the time in years."}]},{"k":"p","text":"To find an unknown, rearrange first and then substitute:"},{"k":"math","tex":"P=\\frac{100I}{rt}\\qquad r=\\frac{100I}{Pt}\\qquad t=\\frac{100I}{Pr}"}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Compound interest","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"**Compound interest** is calculated on the running balance: each year’s interest is added to the principal, and the next year’s interest is earned on this larger amount. Interest begins to earn interest."},{"k":"p","text":"GH₵1,000 at $10\\%$ compound interest becomes GH₵1,100 after one year and $1100\\times1.10=$ GH₵1,210 after two years. The second year earns GH₵110, not GH₵100."},{"k":"fig","id":"w08-stack","caption":"Simple interest adds the same GH₵100 each year. Compound interest adds 10% of the current balance, so it adds more every year."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Compound interest (once a year)","blocks":[{"k":"math","tex":"A=P\\left(1+\\frac{r}{100}\\right)^{n}\\qquad\\qquad\\text{compound interest}=A-P"},{"k":"p","text":"$n$ is the number of years."}]},{"k":"fig","id":"w08-growth","caption":"Over 10 years, simple interest grows in a straight line but compound interest curves upwards."}],"figs":["w08-stack","w08-growth"]},{"title":"Compounding more than once a year","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Banks often compound half-yearly, quarterly or monthly. Then **both** the rate per period and the number of periods change."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Compounding $m$ times a year","blocks":[{"k":"math","tex":"A=P\\left(1+\\frac{r}{100m}\\right)^{mt}"},{"k":"p","text":"Half-yearly: $m=2$. Quarterly: $m=4$. Monthly: $m=12$. Here $r\\%$ is the nominal annual rate and $t$ is in years."}]},{"k":"p","text":"For example, $12\\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly for 18 months gives a rate of $12\\%\\div4=3\\%$ per quarter for $4\\times1.5=6$ quarters."},{"k":"fig","id":"w08-quarters","caption":"Eighteen months is 6 quarters. Each quarter the balance is multiplied by 1.03."},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"Nominal and effective rates","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A rate of $8\\%$ compounded quarterly gives $2\\%$ per quarter. In one year the money is multiplied by $1.02^4\\approx1.0824$, so the **effective** annual rate is about $8.24\\%$, a little more than the nominal $8\\%$."}]}],"figs":["w08-quarters"]},{"title":"Growth factors, depreciation and successive changes","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"The **growth factor** for a $5\\%$ increase is $1.05$; for a $5\\%$ decrease it is $0.95$."},{"k":"p","text":"**Depreciation** is a fall in value over time. If a machine loses $12\\%$ of its **current** value every year, its value after $t$ years is"},{"k":"math","tex":"V=P(0.88)^{t}"},{"k":"p","text":"This is compound decay, not simple interest."},{"k":"fig","id":"w08-depreciation","caption":"Each year the value is 85% of the year before, so the fall in cedis gets smaller each year."},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Successive changes are multiplied","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A $15\\%$ increase followed by a $15\\%$ decrease does **not** return to the original value: $1.15\\times0.85=0.9775$, so the final value is $2.25\\%$ lower than at the start."}]}],"figs":["w08-depreciation"]},{"title":"Interpreting answers","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Real loans can include fees and repayment schedules that change the true cost. Examination questions simplify this, so use exactly the assumptions stated."},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"Rounding money","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Give money to two decimal places (the nearest pesewa). Keep full accuracy in the middle of a calculation and round only at the end."}]},{"k":"box","kind":"life","title":"Where you meet this","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Savings accounts, susu schemes, mobile-money loans, hire purchase and the falling value of a car or a motorbike all use these ideas. Comparing the **final amounts** helps you choose the better offer."}]}],"figs":[]}],"examples":[{"title":"Simple interest for 18 months","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A student deposits GH₵4,800 at $7.5\\%$ simple interest per year for 18 months. Find the interest and the amount."}],"steps":["$P=4800$, $r=7.5$ and $t=\\dfrac{18}{12}=1.5$ years.","$I=\\dfrac{4800\\times7.5\\times1.5}{100}=540$.","$A=P+I=4800+540=5340$."],"answer":"Interest GH₵540; amount GH₵5,340.","figs":[]},{"title":"Finding the principal","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"An investment earned GH₵1,260 simple interest in 3 years at $6\\%$ per annum. Find the principal."}],"steps":["$I=1260$, $r=6$, $t=3$.","$P=\\dfrac{100I}{rt}=\\dfrac{100\\times1260}{6\\times3}=\\dfrac{126000}{18}=7000$.","Check: $6\\%$ of GH₵7,000 is GH₵420 a year, and $3\\times420=1260$ ✓."],"answer":"GH₵7,000","figs":[]},{"title":"A compound interest table","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"GH₵5,000 is invested for 3 years at $8\\%$ per annum compounded annually. Find the amount on GH₵8,000 after 18 months, and the interest earned."}],"steps":["Rate per quarter: $12\\%\\div4=3\\%$, so the factor is $1.03$.","Number of quarters: $4\\times1.5=6$.","$A=8000\\times1.03^6=8000\\times1.1940523\\ldots=9552.42$ (2 d.p.).","Interest: $9552.42-8000=1552.42$."],"answer":"Amount GH₵9,552.42; interest GH₵1,552.42.","figs":[]},{"title":"Simple or compound?","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Compare the interest on GH₵10,000 at $10\\%$ per annum for 2 years under (a) simple interest (b) compound interest, compounded annually."}],"steps":["Simple: $I=\\dfrac{10000\\times10\\times2}{100}=2000$.","Compound: $A=10000\\times1.10^2=12100$, so the interest is $2100$.","Difference: $2100-2000=100$. This is the interest earned in year 2 on the GH₵1,000 interest from year 1."],"answer":"Simple GH₵2,000; compound GH₵2,100. Compounding earns GH₵100 more.","figs":[]},{"title":"Depreciation of a machine","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A machine bought for GH₵24,000 loses $15\\%$ of its value each year. Find the money first invested.","steps":["$A=P\\times1.1^3$, so $6655=1.331P$.","$P=6655\\div1.331=5000$.","Check: $5000\\to5500\\to6050\\to6655$ ✓."],"answer":"GH₵5,000","model":null},{"q":"A student saves GH₵9,000 for 2 years at $8\\%$ per annum. <script type="application/json" id="pack-y1w09">{"year":1,"week":9,"id":"y1w09","title":"Number Patterns, Algebraic Expressions and Factorisation","subtitle":"Turning patterns into general rules; terms, coefficients and like terms; expanding brackets; factorising by common factors, grouping and the difference of two squares.","family":"algebra","section":{"no":2,"name":"Algebra","strand":"Algebraic Reasoning","from":9,"to":12},"outcomes":["Describe a number or shape pattern with a general rule for the $n$th term.","Simplify algebraic expressions by collecting like terms and removing brackets.","Expand products of brackets, including squares of binomials.","Factorise by taking out common factors, by grouping and by the difference of two squares.","Check factorisations by expanding, and use algebra to model real situations."],"keywords":["variable","constant","term","coefficient","like terms","expression","equation","nth term","expand","factorise","grouping","difference of two squares"],"notes":[{"title":"The language of algebra","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"An **algebraic expression** describes a quantity using numbers, letters and operations. A **variable** is a letter that stands for a number that can change or is not yet known; a **constant** is a fixed number."},{"k":"box","kind":"definition","title":"Terms and coefficients","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["A **term** is a part of an expression separated by $+$ or $-$ signs. In $3x^2-5x+7$ the terms are $3x^2$, $-5x$ and $7$.","The **coefficient** is the number multiplying the variable part: the coefficient of $x$ in $-5x$ is $-5$.","Multiplication is often not written: $4ab$ means $4\\times a\\times b$."]}]},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Powers apply only to what they touch","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"$5x^2$ means $5\\times x^2$, but $(5x)^2=5x\\times5x=25x^2$. The bracket tells you that the whole of $5x$ is squared."}]},{"k":"p","text":"An **equation** has an equals sign and states that two expressions are equal, e.g. $3x+1=10$. An **expression** has no equals sign, e.g. $3x+1$. You **simplify** an expression; you **solve** an equation."}],"figs":[]},{"title":"From patterns to general rules","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Patterns help us predict how many objects a growing design needs. Suppose the first three figures have 5, 8 and 11 dots."},{"k":"fig","id":"w09-dots","caption":"Each figure keeps the same 2 grey dots and adds a column of 3 dots, so Figure $n$ has $3n+2$ dots."},{"k":"p","text":"The difference between terms is always $3$, so the rule has the form $T_n=3n+c$. Using $T_1=5$: $3(1)+c=5$, so $c=2$ and"},{"k":"math","tex":"T_n=3n+2"},{"k":"p","text":"Always test the rule on the given figures: $T_2=3(2)+2=8$ ✓ and $T_3=3(3)+2=11$ ✓."},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"The $n$th term of a pattern with a constant difference","blocks":[{"k":"math","tex":"T_n=a+(n-1)d"},{"k":"p","text":"$a$ is the first term and $d$ is the common difference."}]},{"k":"p","text":"When the differences are not constant, look at how the shape grows in two directions. Rectangular arrangements often involve $n(n+1)$ or $n^2$; triangular dot patterns involve $\\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}$."},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"State what $n$ can be","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"In real contexts $n$ is usually a positive whole number (a figure number, a number of seats or of parcels). Say so, because negative or fractional values may make no sense."}]}],"figs":["w09-dots"]},{"title":"Simplifying expressions","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"**Like terms** have exactly the same variable part, including the powers. $7x^2$ and $-2x^2$ are like terms; $7x^2$ and $7x$ are not."},{"k":"math","tex":"6a^2+3a-2a^2+5a=4a^2+8a"},{"k":"p","text":"To remove a bracket, use the **distributive law**: $a(b+c)=ab+ac$."},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Subtracting a bracket","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"A minus sign in front of a bracket changes the sign of **every** term inside:"},{"k":"math","tex":"7x-(3x-4)=7x-3x+4=4x+4"}]}],"figs":[]},{"title":"Expanding products of brackets","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"To multiply two brackets, multiply **every** term in the first bracket by **every** term in the second. A grid keeps the four products organised."},{"k":"fig","id":"w09-grid","caption":"The grid method for $(2x+3)(x-4)$. Each cell is a row term times a column term."},{"k":"math","tex":"(2x+3)(x-4)=2x^2-8x+3x-12=2x^2-5x-12"},{"k":"box","kind":"formula","title":"Useful identities","blocks":[{"k":"ul","items":["$(a+b)^2=a^2+2ab+b^2$","$(a-b)^2=a^2-2ab+b^2$","$(a+b)(a-b)=a^2-b^2$"]}]},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Do not forget the middle term","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"$(x+5)^2=(x+5)(x+5)=x^2+10x+25$, **not** $x^2+25$. We look at perfect squares more closely in Week 10."}]}],"figs":["w09-grid"]},{"title":"Factorisation: the reverse of expansion","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"**Factorising** means writing an expression as a product. Always look for a **common factor** first:"},{"k":"math","tex":"12x^2y-18xy^2=6xy(2x-3y)"},{"k":"p","text":"Check by expanding: $6xy\\times2x=12x^2y$ and $6xy\\times(-3y)=-18xy^2$ ✓."},{"k":"p","text":"**Grouping.** With four terms, pair them so that each pair has a common factor, then take out the common bracket:"},{"k":"math","tex":"ax+ay+bx+by=a(x+y)+b(x+y)=(a+b)(x+y)"},{"k":"fig","id":"w09-grouping","caption":"The four areas $ax$, $ay$, $bx$ and $by$ fit together into one rectangle of width $x+y$ and height $a+b$."},{"k":"p","text":"**Difference of two squares.** A perfect square minus a perfect square factorises as"},{"k":"math","tex":"a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)"},{"k":"p","text":"For example, $9x^2-16=(3x)^2-4^2=(3x-4)(3x+4)$."},{"k":"box","kind":"key","title":"A sum of squares does not factorise this way","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"$9x^2+16$ is a **sum** of two squares. It cannot be factorised into real brackets using this identity."}]},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"Factorising checklist","blocks":[{"k":"ol","items":["Take out the highest common factor.","Two terms: is it a difference of two squares?","Four terms: try grouping (you may need to reorder the terms).","Expand your answer to check that it gives the original expression."]}]}],"figs":["w09-grouping"]},{"title":"Algebra in real life","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Letters make relationships about cost, distance and area easy to work with. The plans cost the same at 4 parcels; after that Plan A is cheaper."},{"k":"p","text":"Check a model by substituting a small value: for $n=1$, $C=20+7=27$ cedis, which matches one delivery of one item."}],"figs":["w09-plans"]}],"examples":[{"title":"A matchstick pattern","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A pattern uses 7 matchsticks in Figure 1, 12 in Figure 2 and 17 in Figure 3, increasing by the same amount each time. Find a rule for the number $M_n$ in Figure $n$, and the first figure that needs more than 100 matchsticks."}],"steps":["The difference is $12-7=5$ and $17-12=5$, so $M_n=5n+c$.","Using $n=1$: $5(1)+c=7$, so $c=2$ and $M_n=5n+2$.","Check: $M_2=12$ ✓ and $M_3=17$ ✓.","Solve $5n+2>100$: $5n>98$, so $n>19.6$.","$n$ is a whole number, so the smallest is $n=20$ ($M_{20}=102$)."],"answer":"$M_n=5n+2$; Figure 20 is the first to need more than 100 matchsticks.","figs":[]},{"title":"Brackets inside brackets","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Simplify $3(2x-5)-2[4-(x+3)]+5x$, and state the coefficient of $x$."}],"steps":["Inner bracket first: $4-(x+3)=4-x-3=1-x$.","Expand: $3(2x-5)=6x-15$ and $-2(1-x)=-2+2x$.","Collect: $6x-15-2+2x+5x=13x-17$."],"answer":"$13x-17$; the coefficient of $x$ is $13$.","figs":[]},{"title":"Expanding and subtracting","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Expand and simplify $(3x-2)(2x+5)-(x-4)^2$."}],"steps":["$(3x-2)(2x+5)=6x^2+15x-4x-10=6x^2+11x-10$.","$(x-4)^2=x^2-8x+16$.","Subtract **every** term: $6x^2+11x-10-x^2+8x-16$.","Collect: $5x^2+19x-26$."],"answer":"$5x^2+19x-26$","figs":[]},{"title":"The highest common factor","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Factorise completely $18a^2b-30ab^2+12ab$."}],"steps":["The HCF of $18$, $30$ and $12$ is $6$, and every term contains $a$ and $b$, so the HCF is $6ab$.","Divide each term by $6ab$: $3a$, $-5b$ and $2$.","So $18a^2b-30ab^2+12ab=6ab(3a-5b+2)$.","Check: $6ab\\times3a=18a^2b$, $6ab\\times(-5b)=-30ab^2$, $6ab\\times2=12ab$ ✓."],"answer":"$6ab(3a-5b+2)$","figs":[]},{"title":"Factorising by grouping","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Factorise $6xy-9x+4y-6$."}],"steps":["Group the terms in pairs: $(6xy-9x)+(4y-6)$.","Take out common factors: $3x(2y-3)+2(2y-3)$.","$(2y-3)$ is now a common factor: $(3x+2)(2y-3)$.","Check: $(3x+2)(2y-3)=6xy-9x+4y-6$ ✓."],"answer":"$(3x+2)(2y-3)$","figs":[]},{"title":"Area of a playground","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"A rectangular playground is $(3x+4)$ m long and $(2x-1)$ m wide. Find a simplified expression for its area, and the area when $x=6$."}],"steps":["Area $=(3x+4)(2x-1)=6x^2-3x+8x-4=6x^2+5x-4$.","When $x=6$: $6(36)+5(6)-4=216+30-4=242$.","Check: the length is $3(6)+4=22$ m and the width is $2(6)-1=11$ m, and $22\\times11=242$ ✓."],"answer":"Area $=6x^2+5x-4$ m²; when $x=6$ the area is $242$ m².","figs":[]},{"title":"Difference of two squares","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Factorise $25p^2-49q^2$. Then use the same identity to find $103^2-97^2$ without long multiplication."}],"steps":["$25p^2=(5p)^2$ and $49q^2=(7q)^2$, so $25p^2-49q^2=(5p-7q)(5p+7q)$.","With $a=103$ and $b=97$: $103^2-97^2=(103-97)(103+97)$.","$=6\\times200=1200$."],"answer":"$(5p-7q)(5p+7q)$; $103^2-97^2=1200$.","figs":[]},{"title":"Comparing two plans","problem":[{"k":"p","text":"Plan A charges GH₵18 per order plus GH₵6 per parcel. Plan B charges GH₵10 per order plus GH₵8 per parcel. Write expressions for the cost of $n$ parcels, find when the costs are equal, and decide which plan is cheaper for 10 parcels."}],"steps":["Plan A: $18+6n$ cedis. Plan B: $10+8n$ cedis ($n$ a whole number).","Equal when $18+6n=10+8n$, so $8=2n$ and $n=4$.","For 10 parcels: A $=18+60=78$ and B $=10+80=90$."],"answer":"The costs are equal at 4 parcels; for 10 parcels Plan A is cheaper by GH₵12.","figs":[]}],"summary":[{"title":"Key results for Week 9","items":["$n$th term of a pattern with common difference $d$: $T_n=a+(n-1)d$.","Like terms have the same variable part; a minus sign before a bracket changes every sign inside.","$(a+b)^2=a^2+2ab+b^2$ and $(a-b)^2=a^2-2ab+b^2$","$a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b)$","Grouping: $ax+ay+bx+by=(a+b)(x+y)$"]}],"quiz":[{"q":"The terms $5x^2$, $-3x$ and $8$ belong to which expression?","options":["$5x^2-3x+8$","$5x^2\\times(-3x)\\times8$","$5(x^2-3x+8)$","$5x^2-3x-8$"],"correct":0,"explain":"Terms are separated by $+$ and $-$ signs: $5x^2$, $-3x$ and $+8$."},{"q":"A pattern is $4,\\ 9,\\ 14,\\ 19,\\ \\ldots$ What is its $n$th term?","options":["$4n+1$","$5n-1$","$5n+1$","$n+4$"],"correct":1,"explain":"$a=4$ and $d=5$: $T_n=4+5(n-1)=5n-1$."},{"q":"Simplify $7x-[3x-(2x-5)]$.","options":["$2x-5$","$6x+5$","$6x-5$","$12x-5$"],"correct":2,"explain":"Inner bracket: $3x-2x+5=x+5$. Then $7x-(x+5)=6x-5$."},{"q":"Expand $(2x+3)(x-4)$.","options":["$2x^2+11x-12$","$2x^2-8x+12$","$2x^2+5x-12$","$2x^2-5x-12$"],"correct":3,"explain":"$2x^2-8x+3x-12=2x^2-5x-12$."},{"q":"Which is the complete factorisation of $12x^2y-18xy^2$?","options":["$6x(2x-3y)$","$6xy(2x-3y)$","$3xy(4x-3y)$","$6xy(2x+3y)$"],"correct":1,"explain":"The HCF is $6xy$, leaving $2x$ and $-3y$."},{"q":"Factorise $9a^2-16$.","options":["$(9a-4)(a+4)$","$(3a-4)^2$","$(3a-4)(3a+4)$","$(3a+4)^2$"],"correct":2,"explain":"It is a difference of two squares: $(3a)^2-4^2$."},{"q":"Which is the correct expansion of $(x-5)^2$?","options":["$x^2-25$","$x^2-10x+25$","$x^2-5x+25$","$x^2+10x+25$"],"correct":1,"explain":"$(a-b)^2=a^2-2ab+b^2$ with $a=x$ and $b=5$."},{"q":"Simplify $4a^2+7a-6a^2+3a$.","options":["$10a^2+10a$","$-2a^2+4a$","$-2a^2+10a$","$2a^2+10a$"],"correct":2,"explain":"$(4-6)a^2+(7+3)a=-2a^2+10a$."},{"q":"Factorise by grouping: $ax+ay+bx+by$.","options":["$(a+x)(b+y)$","$(a+b)(x+y)$","$(a+y)(x+b)$","$(a-b)(x+y)$"],"correct":1,"explain":"$a(x+y)+b(x+y)=(a+b)(x+y)$."},{"q":"A taxi charges GH₵12 plus GH₵5 per kilometre. Whatever you do to one side, you must do to the other side to keep it balanced."},{"k":"fig","id":"w11-balance","caption":"$3x+7=25$: remove 7 from both pans, then share each pan into 3 equal parts, to find $x=6$."},{"k":"p","text":"Undo the operations in reverse order using **inverse operations**: undo $+$ and $-$ first, then $\\times$ and $\\div$."},{"k":"box","kind":"tip","title":"Always check","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Substitute your answer into the **original** equation. For $3x+7=25$: $3(6)+7=25$ ✓."}]}],"figs":["w11-balance"]},{"title":"Changing the subject of a formula","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"To make a variable the subject, list the operations acting on it, then undo them in reverse order, doing the same to both sides."},{"k":"math","tex":"y=mx+c\\ \\Longrightarrow\\ c=y-mx"},{"k":"math","tex":"A=\\tfrac{1}{2}bh\\ \\Longrightarrow\\ 2A=bh\\ \\Longrightarrow\\ h=\\frac{2A}{b}\\quad(b\\neq0)"},{"k":"math","tex":"E=\\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2\\ \\Longrightarrow\\ v^2=\\frac{2E}{m}\\ \\Longrightarrow\\ v=\\sqrt{\\frac{2E}{m}}\\quad(v\\geq0)"},{"k":"box","kind":"note","title":"Square roots in context","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"When you take a square root, there are two values, $\\pm$. This clears all the fractions at once."},{"k":"math","tex":"\\frac{x}{3}-2=\\frac{1}{2}\\quad\\xrightarrow{\\ \\times6\\ }\\quad2x-12=3\\quad\\Longrightarrow\\quad x=\\frac{15}{2}"},{"k":"box","kind":"warn","title":"Multiply every term","blocks":[{"k":"p","text":"Do not forget terms with no denominator. Make $g$ the subject (all quantities are positive).","steps":["Divide by $2\\pi$: $\\dfrac{T}{2\\pi}=\\sqrt{\\dfrac{L}{g}}$.","Square both sides: $\\dfrac{T^2}{4\\pi^2}=\\dfrac{L}{g}$.","Multiply both sides by $4\\pi^2g$, then divide by $T^2$."],"answer":"$g=\\dfrac{4\\pi^2L}{T^2}$","model":null},{"q":"Solve $3(2x+5)-4(x-1)=7x-6$.","steps":["Expand: $6x+15-4x+4=7x-6$.","Simplify: $2x+19=7x-6$.","Add 6 and subtract $2x$: $25=5x$.","Check: $3(15)-4(4)=29$ and $7(5)-6=29$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=5$","model":null},{"q":"Solve the simultaneous equations $3x+2y=19$ and $2x-y=1$.","steps":["Multiply the second equation by 2: $4x-2y=2$.","Add to the first: $7x=21$, so $x=3$.","Substitute: $2(3)-y=1$, so $y=5$.","Check in the first equation: $9+10=19$ ✓."],"answer":"$x=3$, $y=5$","model":null},{"q":"Solve $2-\\dfrac{3x-1}{4}\\leq\\dfrac{x+5}{2}$.","steps":["Multiply every term by 4 (positive): $8-(3x-1)\\leq2(x+5)$.","Expand: $9-3x\\leq2x+10$.","Add $3x$ and subtract 10: $-1\\leq5x$.","Divide by 5: $x\\geq-\\dfrac{1}{5}$ (a filled circle at $-\\dfrac{1}{5}$, shaded to the right)."],"answer":"$x\\geq-\\dfrac{1}{5}$","model":null},{"q":"A bus can carry no more than 75 passengers and already has 18 on board. Groups of 7 passengers are waiting. What is the largest number of whole groups it can still take?","steps":["Let $g$ be the number of groups (a whole number, $g\\geq0$).","$18+7g\\leq75$, so $7g\\leq57$ and $g\\leq\\dfrac{57}{7}\\approx8.14$.","$g$ must be a whole number, so the largest value is $8$.","Check: $18+7\\times8=74\\leq75$, but $18+7\\times9=81>75$."],"answer":"8 groups","model":null}],"checklist":["I can tell the difference between an expression, an equation and a formula.","I can change the subject of a formula, including one with a square or square root.","I can solve equations with brackets and fractions, and check my answer.","I can solve simultaneous equations by elimination and by substitution.","I can solve inequalities, reversing the sign when I multiply or divide by a negative.","I can show a solution set on a number line with open and filled circles."],"plan":{"lessons":[[{"j":0,"notes":true,"exs":[]},{"j":1,"notes":true,"exs":[]},{"j":2,"notes":true,"exs":[0,1]},{"j":3,"notes":true,"exs":[2]},{"j":4,"notes":true,"exs":[3]}],[{"j":5,"notes":true,"exs":[4]},{"j":6,"notes":true,"exs":[]},{"j":7,"notes":true,"exs":[5,6,7]},{"j":8,"notes":true,"exs":[]}]],"exSec":[2,2,3,4,5,7,7,7],"quizSec":[2,7,7,7,7,7,2,7,7,2],"exerSec":[2,7,7,0,7,2,5,7],"thSec":[2,7,5,7,6],"sumSec":[2,4,5,7,7],"chkSec":[0,2,3,5,7,7],"weights":[305.35,732.65,2013.7,944.3,1213.6,1591.6,459.85,3245.3,267.4],"figs":[{"id":"w11-balance","sec":1,"lesson":1,"caption":"$3x+7=25$: remove 7 from both pans, then share each pan into 3 equal parts, to find $x=6$."},{"id":"w11-lines","sec":5,"lesson":2,"caption":"Each equation is a straight line.
